jobs.title: CERN Courier Magazine Associate Editor (SR-ECO-CO-2026-143-GRAP)
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about particle physics? Do you have a flair for a phrase? Would you like to work at the world's leading particle-physics laboratory, communicating the latest developments in high-energy physics to a global audience?
 CERN has an opening for a Project Graduate in the Content section of its Education, Communications and Outreach (ECO) group, within the Stakeholder Relations (SR) sector, to join the editorial team of CERN Courier - the international magazine for high-energy physics, established in 1959.
 CERN Courier magazine  exists to serve the international community working in particle physics and adjacent fields by providing rigorous, accessible and impactful reporting on the latest developments in science, technology and policy.
 Reporting to the CERN Courier editor, you will contribute to the magazine's print and digital editions, showcasing developments in international high-energy physics. This is an ideal opportunity for someone with a background in particle physics who would like to build a career in science communication. Experienced science journalists with a physics background are also encouraged to apply.
 Your responsibilities
 As an associate editor, you will help to drive forward the Courier's print and online presence as part of a small but dynamic team. Your core tasks will include:

• Liaising with the global high-energy physics community to keep the Courier at the forefront of developments in experimental and theoretical particle physics, accelerator physics, astroparticle physics and cosmology.

• Generating ideas, fact checking and proofreading.

• Commissioning and editing expert-authored feature articles.

• Interviewing leading physicists.

• Writing news, features and other articles.

• Curating the cerncourier.com website and managing social media.

• Taking responsibility for the timely production of several sections of the magazine.

• Liaising with publishing partners, partner institutions, authors and readers.

• Collaborating with colleagues across the IR-ECO group to support CERN's communications objectives.

• In addition to developing organisational, communication and editorial skills in an international research laboratory, the successful candidate will gain increased knowledge about high-energy physics, technology and international collaboration in a unique multicultural environment.
 More information here  & here .
 Your profile

• Research experience in high-energy physics or a closely related field.

• Experience in writing, editing and publishing, or the aptitude to rapidly develop these skills.
 Skills

• Communicating complex topics with clarity, accuracy, concision and flair.

• Adapting your communication to the needs of different audiences.

• Knowledge of particle physics and research methodologies.

• The ability to write and edit fluently in English.

• Attention to detail and quality management.

• Service orientation.

• Empathy and active listening.

• Curiosity and independent research.

• Critical and creative thinking.

• Resilience, flexibility and adaptability.

• Time management and prioritisation.

• Motivation and self-awareness.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You have a professional background in Particle Physics, Science Communication (or a related field) and have either:
• a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;

• or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Job closing date: 18.09.2026 at 23:59 CEST.
 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Job flexibility: Fully Onsite
 Target start date: 01-November-2026
 Job reference: SR-ECO-CO-2026-143-GRAP
 Field of work: Communication & Stakeholder Management
 Benchmark job: 5A0020 - Communications/Public Relations /External Relations Professional

Global Benefits

• A monthly net stipend of either 6372 or 7004 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

jobs.title: Junior Test & Measurement Engineer (BE-CEM-MTA-2026-216-GRAE)
jobs.description:
Are you interested in developing measurement, control and monitoring tools that are used on real scientific infrastructure?
 You will join a team working on various measurement instrumentation and control applications used to operate, supervise, and improve CERN systems. You will contribute to the development and evolution of software built with LabVIEW and Python, supporting both existing operational tools and new developments. This includes applications used for vacuum measurements, data logging, gas analysis and the integration of instrumentation into CERN's control environment. The role also includes work related to new installations and upgrades, where reliable monitoring, automation and safe operation are essential.
 This is an opportunity to work close to equipment, users and experts, and to contribute to tools that are directly relevant for daily operation, commissioning and future upgrades. You will gain practical experience in measurement, controls, software integration, instrumentation and test environments, while learning CERN working methods and standards in a highly collaborative setting.
 Your responsibilities

• Develop and maintain applications for monitoring and control of vacuum instrumentation using LabVIEW and Python.

• Contribute to software used with gas analysers, pressure gauges and related vacuum equipment.

• Improve tools for acquisition, logging, analysis and visualisation of various data.

• Participate in the integration of new instruments and new functionalities into the existing control infrastructure.

• Support testing, validation and deployment of software on operational systems.

• Work with engineers, technicians and users to translate operational needs into robust software solutions.

• Document developments, configurations and procedures on the team's internal documentation platforms.

• Support installed applications and participate in their follow-up and maintenance.
 More information here .
 Your profile

• Initial experience programming in Python.

• Keen interest in the integration of scientific and industrial instrumentation, data acquisition, analysis and control systems.

• Initial experience developing applications in LabVIEW would be an advantage.
 Skills

• LabVIEW; LabVIEW Real-Time and/or FPGA knowledge is an advantage.

• Python.

• Knowledge of Linux environments.

• Structured, rigorous & autonomous working style.

• Interest in multidisciplinary teamwork in an international environment.

• Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Software, Electrical/Electronics Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree .

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

• Applicants without University degree are not eligible.

• Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Job closing date: 21.09.2026 at 23:59 CEST.
 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Working hours: 40 hours per week
 Job flexibility: Fully Onsite
 Target start date: 01-November-2026
 This position involves:

• Work in Radiation Areas.

• Interventions in underground installations.

• A valid driving licence.
 Job reference: BE-CEM-MTA-2026-216-GRAE
 Field of work: Electronics Engineering
 Benchmark job: 200020 - Computing Engineer

Global Benefits

• A monthly net stipend of either 5266 or 5793 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

• Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances.

• A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances.

• Possibility to extend your contract up to 36 months.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Are you interested in developing measurement, control and monitoring tools that are used on real scientific infrastructure?
You will join a team working on various measurement instrumentation and control applications used to operate, supervise, and improve CERN systems. You will contribute to the development and evolution of software built with LabVIEW and Python, supporting both existing operational tools and new developments. This includes applications used for vacuum measurements, data logging, gas analysis and the integration of instrumentation into CERN's control environment. The role also includes work related to new installations and upgrades, where reliable monitoring, automation and safe operation are essential.
This is an opportunity to work close to equipment, users and experts, and to contribute to tools that are directly relevant for daily operation, commissioning and future upgrades. You will gain practical experience in measurement, controls, software integration, instrumentation and test environments, while learning CERN working methods and standards in a highly collaborative setting.
Your responsibilities

• Develop and maintain applications for monitoring and control of vacuum instrumentation using LabVIEW and Python.

• Contribute to software used with gas analysers, pressure gauges and related vacuum equipment.

• Improve tools for acquisition, logging, analysis and visualisation of various data.

• Participate in the integration of new instruments and new functionalities into the existing control infrastructure.

• Support testing, validation and deployment of software on operational systems.

• Work with engineers, technicians and users to translate operational needs into robust software solutions.

• Document developments, configurations and procedures on the team's internal documentation platforms.

• Support installed applications and participate in their follow-up and maintenance.
More information here .
Your profile

• Initial experience programming in Python.

• Keen interest in the integration of scientific and industrial instrumentation, data acquisition, analysis and control systems.

• Initial experience developing applications in LabVIEW would be an advantage.
Skills

• LabVIEW; LabVIEW Real-Time and/or FPGA knowledge is an advantage.

• Python.

• Knowledge of Linux environments.

• Structured, rigorous & autonomous working style.

• Interest in multidisciplinary teamwork in an international environment.

• Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Software, Electrical/Electronics Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree .

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

• Applicants without University degree are not eligible.

• Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.
